title: Kleftiko
subtitle: Greek slow-roasted lamb shoulder sealed in paper
excerpt: The Greek celebration dish: lamb shoulder marinated in lemon, garlic, and oregano, then sealed inside a parcel of greaseproof paper and roasted very slowly until the meat falls from the bone in tender, fragrant shreds. The sealed parcel traps all the steam and juices.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kleftiko (the name means stolen or cooked by thieves) is a celebrated Greek dish of lamb slow-roasted in a sealed vessel. The legend holds that the klephts, the Greek mountain brigands of the Ottoman period, cooked their (often stolen) meat in underground pits covered with earth so the smoke would not betray them. Whether or not the history is accurate, the technique of sealing the meat so it cooks in its own steam and juices is genuinely ancient, and the result is dramatically different from open-roasted lamb. Sealed in greaseproof paper or foil, the lamb steams and braises in its own moisture and the lemon, garlic, and oregano marinade; the paper is opened at the table so the scented steam escapes in front of the diners.

recipeTools.notes: A large roasting tin with enough room for the paper parcel.

content.text: The longer and lower the better: 4 hours at 160 C (140 C fan) produces more tender lamb than 2 hours at 190 C. Cut slits deep into the lamb and push garlic slices all the way in. Seal the paper parcel completely with no gaps; any steam that escapes will dry the meat. Open the parcel for the final 20 minutes to colour the surface.

items.preparation: bone-in; ask the butcher to score the skin
half sliced for stuffing, half roughly crushed

content.text: Cut 12 deep slits all over the lamb shoulder. Push a slice of garlic deep into each slit. Mix the lemon zest, lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, crushed garlic, salt, and pepper. Rub the marinade all over the lamb, getting it into the slits. If time allows, marinate in the fridge for up to 24 hours.

Heat the oven to 160 C (140 C fan). Lay a large double sheet of greaseproof paper in a roasting tin. Put the potatoes in the centre and season them. Place the lamb on top. Bring the paper up around the lamb and seal the edges tightly by folding them over several times. If needed, use a second sheet to reinforce.

Roast for 3 hours 30 minutes. Open the parcel carefully (hot steam) and fold back the paper. Increase the oven to 200 C (180 C fan) and cook for a further 20 to 30 minutes until the lamb is lightly coloured on top. The meat should fall apart when pressed with a spoon. Serve from the paper, tearing the meat at the table.
